title: ia init --migrate rewrites a 1.1.0 starter workspace into the three starter records, installing the bundled language base where it has a 1.x one, then captures it and re-projects its registered hosts
summary: ia init --migrate [--system] [--apply] [--json] [--yes] (new) takes a workspace a 1.1.0 ia init created (1.0 and 1.1 write the same starter): one folder in .ia/src/systems/, its local system <name>, holding only system.ia, with exactly `@system <name>`, which registers no word, and `@agent <name>-steward`, and records/*.ia, of which records/workspace.ia holds exactly `@workspace <name>` and `@distribution <name>-distribution`, the distribution .ia/release.json names. The three starter records use fields only the language base this CLI bundles declares (composition.sources, composition.steward and the `@mandate`'s authority section), so where the installed inventarch/language is another archive, as in every workspace a published 1.x CLI initialized, the migration installs the bundled one in its place, offline as ia init installs it, which needs a lock holding that one base alone. It plans by default and writes nothing, and plan and apply run one preflight first. Customized workspace or distribution starter meaning, answers, comments, relationships or distribution declarations are refused before writes instead of silently replaced; edits to the workspace composition.systems list remain supported. Kept records that refer to a steward, system or distribution a plain migration would remove are conflicts, with --system as the preservation path. Any other shape (a nested folder, another file, another record in system.ia or records/workspace.ia, a local `@system` that registers words, a second system folder, a descriptor naming no distribution or another one, a base to replace in a lock that holds other packages) is refused as IA-CLI-CONFLICT (exit 3) naming ia init --help; a workspace that does not admit is refused as IA-CLI-CONFLICT naming ia validate --root <root>; and, with a host projection registered, a pending host journal is refused with its own code, located at the journal, naming its ia-distribution recovery, then the rerun. A destination that already exists (.ia/src/workspace.ia, or .ia/src/<file>.ia for a moved file), a record the workspace keeps that already holds `@agent <name>` or `@mandate <name>-mandate`, which would tie with the new records, and a registered projection whose guard retirement or file plan the planners refuse, such as a file without a marker at a target path, are listed as conflicts by the plan (exit 0), and --apply refuses them with nothing written: a collision as IA-CLI-CONFLICT naming ia init <directory> --migrate, a projection conflict alone with the planner's code, located at its file, naming ia host <host> --root <root>. The plan lists the base install, every move, write and delete, the folders the migration leaves empty included, and each registered host's guard retirement and file actions, planned for the migrated records, whose new revision every rendered file carries, so none is reported unchanged. --apply records its owned paths and exact before/after content digests in .ia/migration.json before mutation, then installs the bundled base where the plan says so while the records are still 1.1.0-shaped. A retry verifies those recorded bytes, recognizes its own partly completed operations and resumes them; an unexpected edit is a conflict, not permission to overwrite foreign work. It then moves every other records/<file>.ia byte for byte to .ia/src/<file>.ia, where each record keeps its identity because a record's word, not its folder, decides its system; writes .ia/src/workspace.ia with the three records ia init writes, keeping the 1.1.0 `@workspace` name and composition.systems and adding composition.sources and composition.steward; writes .ia/.gitignore where none exists, retaining work/ but omitting distributions/ when the installation payload is already tracked by Git so its replacement stays visible to commits; an existing ignore file is preserved; deletes records/workspace.ia, system.ia and the three folders they leave empty; and rewrites .ia/release.json without distribution and with the bundled base's dependency row in place of the installed base's, keeping every other row. For tracked installations, preflight checks every required store, generation, active-pointer and portable-lock path against effective Git ignore and byte-conversion rules. A hidden required file or text/eol/filter/encoding conversion refuses before writes, naming the offending ignore rule or the .gitattributes repair. Git configuration, the index, existing ignores and attributes remain unchanged. With --system it keeps system.ia as it is, writes records/distribution.ia rooted at [`@system <name>`] as ia init --system does, composes the local system and keeps the descriptor's distribution, so ia pack still builds, leaving the descriptor byte for byte, whatever its formatting, when its base row is already the bundled base's. It then captures the workspace and re-projects each host whose projection state exists through the projection apply ia host uses, which retires the 1.1.0 steward guard, deletes the owned steward agent files and writes the receipt ia doctor reads. The journal remains until files, admission, capture and registered-host projections complete. Nothing is rolled back: a file failure names repair of the reported filesystem problem and the same ia init <directory> --migrate [--system] --apply --yes command to finish; failures or interruptions after capture or projection also retain the journal and name that migration resume command. A pending host journal first names its matching ia-distribution recovery, then the migration resume. A migrated workspace that fails admission names ia validate --root <root>, saying neither effect ran, and the journal retains its recovery state. With --json the plan holds migrate (1.1.0), id, name, system, base ({id, installed, bundled}), conflicts, steps, moves, writes, records, systems, removes (the empty folders as <path>/ rows with no identities), ignore, descriptor ({path, before, after, dependencies}) and hosts, and applied is {status: migrated, id, base (installed or present), distribution, authored, moved, removed, ignore, effects: {capture, project: [{host, files, receipt, guard, removed}]}}. --id, --host and the decline options beside --migrate are usage (exit 2). @inventarch/cli/internal/init adds collectMigration (taking the package root whose base it installs), applyMigration (async), migrationEnvelope, renderMigration, renderMigrated and MIGRATES_FROM with their types. For a fresh clone with an empty cache, ia restore can seed the CLI's verified bundled language archive only when its id, version, archive digest and manifest digest exactly match the lock, with or without --offline; an exact unpublished bundled pin needs no registry lookup. A different locked archive keeps the existing restore path. Limits: only the 1.1.0 starter shape is recognized, so a workspace that grew past it in any of the refused ways above is migrated by hand, as is one whose 1.x base shares its lock with another installed package; another package installed beside the bundled base is kept, and the descriptor's other dependency rows are always kept; a 1.x record the bundled base does not admit stops the base install before any record file is written; projection conflicts found before migration name ia host <host> to inspect the registered host's plan; once migration has begun, interruption and effect repairs resume the same ia init <directory> --migrate [--system] --apply --yes command after any required host-journal recovery; the steward guard stays retired; workspace revisions of unchanged sources, the nine machine routes, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2, every ia scope form, body(K) and ia.position-body.v1 are unchanged.
